observed.facings.png: A single south picture of a rusty grey-steel pump set on wooden skids. On the left is a centrifugal pump body with a short vertical riser whose top flange is seen as an ellipse with its bore showing. A grey electric motor with cooling fins sits on the right on a timber frame, braced with a diagonal plank. Mismatched rust-brown patch plates are riveted on, and rope is lashed around the riser and the right end of the manifold. A large horizontal pipe runs across the front from west to east. At its west end an elbow rises into the pump. Both manifold ends finish in heavy bolted flanges drawn as near-round discs turned toward the viewer, with dark open bores clearly visible. No stub or coupler is drawn at the bottom centre.
observed.south.png: The same picture at full resolution on transparency, with the same content as facings.png. The manifold end flanges at the left (~x95,y515) and right (~x670,y510) are about 70 px wide and 95 px tall, tilted about three-quarters toward the camera, with dark bores showing. The riser's top flange is a flat ellipse about 0.5 as tall as wide, with its lit top visible. The pump body, motor and manifold are mostly drawn as a front elevation. The cut-out is clean, with no ground patch or cast shadow.
observed.scale.png: The station on a brown backdrop beside a vanilla human at the same scale. The station is about 2.5–3 cells wide and well under 3 cells tall, so it sits low in its 3x3 footprint. It looks proportionate to the pawn as a ground machine.
observed.siblings.png: An in-game capture of the 'repaired' look: a cream-white pipe manifold with red handwheel valves and a dark motor, a similar layout, with a hose coming down from the bottom centre. At this size its manifold ends read as rounded elbows or caps rather than wide open bores facing the camera.
observed.assembled_1.png: In-game capture on grassland. The station sits with its manifold ends showing large open bores toward the camera on both west and east. A short grey stub with a brass coupler comes down from below the bottom centre of the manifold, and a wrapped hose runs south from it. A separate hose end lies loose about two cells east of the east flange and is not connected. Nothing is attached to the west port. A yellow power-off bolt overlays the pump.
observed.assembled_2.png: A closer crop of the same scene. The two manifold flanges read as round pipe mouths aimed at the viewer, so the pipe seems to bend up toward the camera at both ends, even though it lies along the ground running west-east. The south stub and brass coupler sit at the bottom centre, partly behind the wooden skid. The loose east hose end lies off to the right, unconnected.

BORE.seen: Both west and east ends of the horizontal manifold show wide open bores toward the camera, although the pipe lies along the ground running west-east and does not turn toward the viewer. The riser-top bore is legitimate.

PORTS.seen: The south hose meets the brass coupler on the stub at the bottom centre at the same cell. No hose is connected to the west or east port in either capture: the east hose end lies loose about two cells away. The side ports cannot be judged.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: The west and east manifold ends each carry a drawn flange connector. The south stub and brass coupler appear at the bottom centre in the assembled view. No extra connector is drawn apart from the riser top flange, which is the description's riser rather than a hose port. The riser top flange is ambiguous, but the description names it.

LAYERS.seen: The south stub emerges from behind or under the manifold and skid, and the hose draws below it. Nothing that should be in front is hidden.

ROTATIONS.seen: Graphic_Single: one picture for every rotation, by design.

SIGNATURE.seen: All the described parts are recognisable: riser with top flange, front manifold running west-east, borrowed electric motor, mismatched patch plates, rope lashings and timber skids. The south stub and coupler are supplied in game.

MATERIAL.seen: Rusted cast steel, worn timber and hemp rope read as materials, not paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: About 650×446 px of a 768 canvas, centred, sitting low in the 3x3 footprint without overflow.

ALPHA.seen: Clean alpha. Measured real alpha is present, with no backdrop or painted shadow.

OURS.seen: Bespoke kludged art with mismatched plates and rope. It does not match any vanilla or donor sprite.

LEGIBLE.seen: In assembled_1 at near-normal zoom, the motor, riser and manifold read clearly as a pump station.

subject: RM_HoseFreeEnd_Mouth

reply.subject: RM_HoseFreeEnd_Mouth

observed.facings.png: One enlarged panel labelled south. It shows a full circle on a checkerboard (real alpha): a wide, dark brown-grey rim around an almost black, slightly oval bore. Shading is flat, with only a faint darker inner edge. It is a hole seen straight on, as if looking down the barrel of a pipe.
observed.south.png: A 64 px version of the same thing: a dark brown ring around a black hole, seen face-on. The background is transparent.
observed.scale.png: An in-game capture of three 2x2 reels (red Modern at top, black Industrial in the middle, rusty Scrapper at the bottom) at about 132 px/cell, with a vanilla human at the same scale. Each reel's hose runs right into a separate tip panel. Modern: a cream fabric hose ending in a chrome band coupling, with a small dark oval hole on the coupling's right end face. Industrial: a black corrugated hose with a hazard-striped band, ending in a black oval hole at the right end. Scrapper: a brown hose wrapped in tan cloth, angled up and to the right, ending in a dark oval hole. In all three the end of the hose shows its open bore as a vertical ellipse facing the viewer and the right side.
observed.variants_1.png: Industrial look: a black ring with fine concentric ribbing around a black hole, face-on.
observed.variants_2.png: Modern look: a pale cream/grey ring with a dark outline around a black hole, face-on.
observed.variants_3.png: Futuristic look: a dark ring with cyan glowing segments and light dots around a black hole, face-on.
observed.assembled_1.png: A tighter crop of the same three reels and their tip panels. The free ends are clearer: each hose ends with a vertical dark ellipse on its outer face (Modern on the chrome coupling, Industrial on the black rubber cuff, Scrapper on the cloth wrap). The ellipse reads as looking into the open pipe.
observed.assembled_2.png: A wide in-game frame. The red reel's cream hose runs about 9 cells east to a chrome coupling tip, and the black reel's corrugated hose runs east to a striped tip with a small dark end. The rust reel is cut off at the bottom. At this zoom the mouths are a few dark pixels at the hose tips.
observed.assembled_3.png: A kludged rusty pump station on grass. Its horizontal pipe ends show full round flange bores facing the camera (that is the pump's art, not this subject). At the right edge, a cloth-wrapped brown hose comes in from the right, angled down and to the left, and ends in a dark oval bore facing the viewer.

CAMERA.seen: The hose bodies around the mouth read as cylinders lying on the ground under the building camera, with lit tops and the body foreshortened. The mouth's own plane is judged under BORE.

BORE.seen: Each free end shows an open dark bore on its end face as a vertical ellipse, although the hose lies flat and points east, or roughly east-northeast and west-southwest. The camera tilts only in the north-south plane, so the end face of an east-pointing horizontal hose is edge-on and its inside cannot be seen. The bore implies the tip is turned up toward the viewer.

PORTS.seen: In every capture the mouth sits exactly at the hose's terminal face, at the same height and along the hose axis. It follows the hose's angle on the Scrapper and in the assembled_3 hose.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: The one code port (the free end) has a drawn mouth at the hose tip, and there are no other drawn connectors on the free-end piece.

LAYERS.seen: The mouth draws over the hose end and the wrap or coupling, with nothing wrongly in front of it.

ROTATIONS.seen: There is one texture per look, rotated along the hose. Scrapper, Industrial, Modern and Futuristic share the same ring-and-hole structure, each in its family's palette.

SIGNATURE.seen: The open cut end of a hose is recognisable as such at each tip.

MATERIAL.seen: Dark rubber and fabric rims on Scrapper and Industrial, a cream or chrome-matched ring on Modern, and a dark ring with cyan inlay on Futuristic. They read as material.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The mouth is squashed to 0.30 x 0.86 hose widths and stays within the hose's end. It neither overflows nor floats.

ALPHA.seen: south.png and the variants have real alpha around the ring, with no backdrop or shadow.

OURS.seen: Simple custom ring textures matched to the four GSS looks. I see no sign of donor art.

LEGIBLE.seen: At normal zoom (assembled_2) the tip reads as a dark-ended hose cut, a few pixels wide. That is enough to read as an open end.

reply.needs_call_why: The card puts this exact question under review. The verdict depends on whether a squashed face-on bore at the tip is the same error the owner described for Reel_Deployed_north. I judge it to be: with the camera tilt purely north-south, the end face of an east-pointing hose is edge-on. A second reader should confirm this geometry.
proposals: Add a geometry note to the hose module: for a hose lying flat, the end face's visible height is |sin(heading toward south)| times the hose diameter. East and west ends are edge-on and show no bore; north-pointing ends show the outer wall; only south-pointing ends show the bore. The C# squash (0.30) could then be driven by the hose heading instead of being fixed.
The pump station in assembled_3 shows horizontal flange outlets as full face-on bores, which looks like the same BORE_PLANE / CAM_WRONG pattern. Queue that pump for its own review.
